correctness.rationale: For a faithful C_r⋊C_m with r prime and m|r−1, every element x^a y^b outside the kernel has b≠0 and lies in a unique conjugate complement because 1-u^b is invertible mod r. Thus the r complements intersect only at 1, every nontrivial cyclic subgroup outside the kernel lies in exactly one complement, and the normal C_r has no cyclic overgroup and is a leaf. The graph is therefore r copies of C(C_m)^* glued at 1 plus the kernel leaf. This gives |C(G)|=2+r(τ(m)−1) and |E|=1+r e(m). Since gcd(r,m)=1, the cyclic comparison has τ(m)+2e(m) edges. Finally e(m)≥τ(m)−1 because the cyclic-subgroup graph of C_m is connected, and r≥5, so (r−2)e(m)−(τ(m)−1)>0. The inspected verifier builds the semidirect products directly and checks representative cases, but the proof is group-theoretic and universal.

The theorem excludes the m=2 dihedral boundary and does not cover arbitrary Frobenius kernels.

originality.rationale: Tărnăuceanu's theorem leaves the relevant even nonnilpotent regime conjectural. Cameron–Reddy–Sharma treat ordinary dihedral, dicyclic, generalized quaternion, nilpotent, and minimal non-cyclic families; their inspected minimal-noncyclic semidirect products are not the faithful even-complement Frobenius family here (except excluded boundary phenomena). Resultary searches found no prior cyclic-subgroup-graph decomposition for faithful prime-kernel Frobenius groups with arbitrary even cyclic complement m≥4. The exact one-point-union structure and strict edge comparison therefore survive as original to the best of current evidence.
